Commentary.Commentary: We are back! Welcome back for Sri Lanka's reply. The two umpires and the English players have made their way out to the middle. Nishan Madushka and Dimuth Karunaratne stride out to open their innings. Chris Woakes will kickstart proceedings with the new ball for England. Away we go...
... SECOND INNINGS ...

Sri Lanka, on the other hand, will be disappointed as they started pretty well with the ball, but just could not pick up wickets at regular intervals and conceded a few big partnerships as well. Asitha Fernando was the pick of the bowlers with his fantastic five-wicket haul while Milan Rathnayake and Lahiru Kumara chipped in with a couple of wickets each. Prabath Jayasuriya also picked up one, but they only have themselves to blame as they could have kept the hosts well under 400 or even under 350. Now, the batters need to take up a lot of responsibility to get close to this total. Join us in a bit for the Lankan reply.

A splendid batting performance from England finally comes to an end! Joe Root was obviously the standout batter for them with his incredible knock of 143 off 206 balls, but Gus Atkinson came in as the surprise package for Sri Lanka. He smashed his way to his maiden Test hundred and that helped the hosts to go past the 400-run mark. A few of their batters also got off to starts notably, Ben Duckett and Harry Brook while the lower order also contributed well. The bowlers have enough runs to play with and, they will want to keep the Lankans to as low as possible.

Commentary.Commentary: In all readiness for the action on Day 2 to begin! The two umpires stride out to the middle, followed by the Lankans as they take their positions. Gus Atkinson and Matthew Potts are on their way to the crease to resume their innings for England. Lahiru Kumara will get the job to start the proceeding for Sri Lanka. Let's play...

Sri Lanka’s bowlers will look to bounce back on Day 2 after a tiring first day in the field. They started well, taking three wickets in the first 19 overs, but the middle order slowed their momentum. They couldn’t capitalize even with the new ball after the 80th over. With a new day ahead, the bowlers will come out refreshed, aiming to take the remaining three wickets. Stay tuned as the action is about to resume!

England will be pleased with how they ended Day 1, recovering well after a shaky start. Once again, the middle order showed resilience, anchoring the innings and boosting the score. Ben Duckett was the only top-order player to make an impact, but Joe Root remains at the crease, having played a superb knock of 143 runs from 206 balls. The lower middle order, particularly Gus Atkinson and Matthew Potts, added vital runs, with Atkinson achieving his highest Test score. Expect England to play aggressively today to build their advantage and try to go over the 400-run mark to put Sri Lanka under more pressure.

Hello and welcome to Day 2 of this thrilling second Test between England and Sri Lanka at the iconic Lord's Cricket Ground in London. With the game currently tilting in England's favor, we’re set for an action-packed day of Test cricket that could be crucial. The weather looks favorable, promising another full day of play, just like Day 1.
... DAY 2, SESSION 1 ...

Right then, that is it from an exciting Day 1 of this 2nd Test. England have the upper hand and will want to keep the pressure on the visitors. Sri Lanka will need their batters to step up to challenge the hosts. Day 2 will begin on 30th August, Friday at 10 am GMT, but you can join us early for all the build-up. Cheers!

Sri Lanka went into the final session in a good position but standing on their way was Root as they threw everything at him, but nothing broke him down. Not only that, but he went on to equal the record of Alastair Cook for most centuries by an English batter in Tests. Woakes couldn't stick around for long as Kumara sent him back, but Root was just on another level. He also found a good partner in Gus Atkinson who is mainly known for his bowling, but came in and attacked the Lankans from ball one and forced his way to his highest individual Test score. Together, they were racking up the runs quite quickly and added 92 runs in no time which pushed the total over 300. Just as they were looking all settled, Root went for his trademark reverse scoop but lost his wicket in the process on 143 runs. Atkinson soon notched up his maiden Test half-century and the hosts have the early advantage in this game. Atkinson remained unbeaten on 74 while Potts also added crucial 20 runs towards the end.

The second session saw Root and Brook upping the scoring rate, looking comfortable at the crease. However, their momentum was halted when Fernando trapped Brook LBW, ending his promising start. Root, unaffected by his partner's departure, continued to bat with confidence, enjoying a bit of luck along the way. He reached his 65th Test fifty and then shifted gears, playing more aggressively. Jamie Smith, who has impressed since his debut, struggled initially but managed to play some attractive shots before being dismissed by Milan Rathnayake. Root and Smith's partnership added 62 runs, bringing England's total close to 200 as the teams headed into the Tea break.

After winning the toss, Sri Lanka made a surprising decision to bowl first, as teams generally prefer to bat at Lord's. However, the Sri Lankan pacers made the most of the conditions, securing an early breakthrough. Lahiru Kumara set the tone by forcing a nick from Dan Lawrence, justifying his inclusion in the match. Asitha Fernando then dismissed England's skipper, who never looked settled at the crease. Joe Root came in and looked solid from the outset, forming a steady partnership with Ben Duckett. However, Duckett's attempt to take on the spinner led to his dismissal. Jayasuriya was brought in for a single over, and it paid off as Duckett, after getting a good start, was caught on 40, leaving him disappointed at missing the opportunity to convert it into a bigger score. Despite this, Root and Harry Brook ensured there were no further losses before Lunch, stabilizing England's innings.

After being put in to bat, England faced some early challenges, mainly with batters failing to convert their starts into significant scores. However, the positive was that the scoreboard kept moving, largely thanks to Joe Root ​​​​​​'s brilliant form. Root navigated through the tough periods and was the standout performer on Day 1, showcasing his class with a superb innings and reaching his 33rd Test century. Sri Lanka started strong with the ball but gradually lost their edge as the day progressed, allowing England to capitalize and push their total well past 300, with Root making a whopping 143.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the third and final session on Day 1! The umpires have taken their places out in the middle as the Lankan players stride out to the middle. Chris Woakes and Joe Root are all set to resume their stay. Prabath Jayasuriya will be bowling the first over after the Tea break. Lets play...
... DAY 1, SESSION 3 ...

Right then! The Lankan bowlers have cleaned half of the opposition's batting unit and they would love to wrap things up as quickly as possible. But will the English batters shape themselves to go all guns out after the Tea break? Or, will they would be looking to pursue their partnership for the next couple of hours and survive till the end of the day? Stay tuned, as an enthralling final session on Day 1 will start at 3.00 pm GMT.

Lankan bowlers were trying all sorts of spells but nothing was favoring them. They got a couple of edges but the English batters were riding their luck. However, the story didn't continue as it was rolling, and all thanks to Milan Rathnayake. He caught Smith off guard and eliminated him off the pitch in the 49th over.

After the arrival of Jamie Smith on the track, the intent from England was clear as water and the instruction was not to lose any more wickets till the end of the session. They started their passive approach and kept their composure on track. In the meantime, Root successfully bagged his 65th half-century in Test cricket and continued to circulate the scoreboard. They both did an exceptional job of picking the score from 130 for 4 to 192 and formed a sturdy partnership of 62 runs.

Session Summary - 103 runs, 29 overs, and 2 wickets. Just after the Lunch break, Harry Brook survived a run out in the very first over. However, that incident shook both the batters pretty well to hold their focus on communicating better. They looked good and were stroking a couple of boundaries in regular intervals, but the change of end from Asitha Fernando worked like a treat to hunt Brook down.
Pitched up again, on middle, Chris Woakes is solid in his defense again. THAT WILL BE TEA ON DAY 1!

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the post-Lunch session on Day 1! The umpires are out in the middle and so are the players of Sri Lanka. Joe Root is all set to resume his stay on the crease alongside Harry Brook. It will be Lahiru Kumara who will get proceedings underway with the ball after the interval. Let's play...
... DAY 1, SESSION 2 ...

Sri Lanka bowled well, they managed to take wickets at regular intervals. Except for Rathnayake, every bowler has a wicket at least. They would want to keep chipping away at the wickets. The second session we believe will be a lot better to bat so Lanka will have to be patient and hit the right lines and lengths. An important second session coming up at 12.40 GMT.

SESSION SUMMARY - 97 runs, 24 overs and 3 wickets! A good session of Test cricket! Sri Lanka will be happy with the three wickets they’ve got but England will be pleased with the rate they have scored at. Duckett batted freely, he scored at a brisk rate but Pope and Lawrence couldn’t hang around with him. Root and the opener then put up a good stand to get the innings back on track but that was broken too as Duckett fell 10 short of a half-ton. Root though is set now and Brooks has looked solid. England will hope the two can put up a good partnership and lay a good platform for a big first innings score.

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness now! The sun is out here at Lord's and it is the perfect English weather, great for a Test match. Ben Duckett and Dan Lawrence are the openers for England. Asitha Fernando has the new red cherry in his hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

Just moments away from the start of the 2nd Test, but before that, the players from both sides make their way out to the middle and line up for their respective national anthems. It will be Sri Lanka's first followed by the national anthem of England.

Ollie Pope, the captain of England says that they would have batted anyway. Adds that when you are in Lord's, you look up and then look down, that's what they say. Mentions that they are happy to bat and got what they wanted in both games. Ends by saying that the conditions are slightly different, more English and quicker outfield.

Dhananjaya de Silva, the skipper of Sri Lanka says that there is always swing in the first hour. Adds that Pathum Nissanka has been in good form in white-ball cricket. Mentions that they need to pick up 20 wickets to win and they have brought in Lahiru Kumara for his experience. Ends by saying that they need to execute better in this Test.

Sri Lanka left Old Trafford disheartened, but they put up a good fight against England. Their top order needs to show more resilience after being easily dismissed by the English pacers. Experienced players like Angelo Mathews and Kusal Mendis bring stability to the batting lineup, while captain Dhananjaya de Silva aims to continue his good form. The standout is Kamindu Mendis, who has already scored three centuries in just four Test matches. Despite concerns over their bowling, Asitha Fernando impressed with six wickets in the first match, and Prabath Jayasuriya made a strong impact with his spin. Sri Lanka will be looking for better support from the rest of the bowlers to turn things around. Can they finally secure a Test win against England after a decade, or will the hosts clinch the series? The excitement is building as we await the toss.

Despite missing Ben Stokes due to a recent injury, England managed to secure victory in the first match under the leadership of Ollie Pope. However, Pope faces a new challenge as Mark Wood has also been sidelined with an injury, leading to his replacement. While fans will miss the experience of the veteran pacer, they are eager to see Olly Stone make his comeback after three years. Chris Woakes was in fine form, taking three wickets in each innings, and Matthew Potts showed resilience, particularly in the final innings. England's batting lineup is strong, with aggressive openers Ben Duckett and Dan Lawrence looking to put pressure on the opposition. Although Pope didn’t shine in the first match, the middle order, anchored by Jamie Smith’s 150-run performance, held firm. With only one change in their bowling lineup, it will be interesting to see how England strategizes for another win.
